note: AMBUSH. The battered blue heavyweight: weathered sky-blue plate over
bare metal, a bright steel helmet, chrome forearm pistons, an amber
pair of marks across the chest, and fists that have lost their paint
entirely. Painted off the reference photograph.
HE IS NOT IN A T-POSE. The rig is stored in a boxing stance — arms
down and forward, weight on the front foot — so `ax` is not the
distance along an arm here the way it is on a dressed character. It
does not need to be: LIMBS asks the skeleton which part a vertex is,
and that answer is the same in any pose. Only the heights within one
limb are read off the stance, and they were measured, not guessed:
THERE IS NO HEAD BONE WITH ANYTHING ON IT. Every vertex of his helmet
is weighted to Neck, so limbOf calls the whole head `neck` and the
face overlay — which only ever runs on `head` — can never fire. That
is fine for this one: his face is a steel visor with no screen and no
eyes, and a step at 0.86 divides the throat from the helmet exactly
as well.
THE CHEVRON IS A DECAL AND NOT A BAND, because a band is a height and
a height goes round the back too. Two marks either side of the
centreline, which is what the reference has, fall out of one decal
with a gap in its `ax` range.
THE RUST IS THE POINT. Flat blue with the cavity term on it is a toy;
what makes the photograph read as this robot is the bare metal coming
through in patches, heaviest on the edges. See WEATHER.
